It serves affordable Asian-Indonesian comfort food (fried rice, noodles, kwetiau, chicken and seafood dishes) famous for huge "jumbo" portions at Rp23k–55k, targeting middle-class families and mall shoppers. samwumed.org zoominfo.com/c/samwumed/346685548 SAMWUMED (founded 1952, Cape Town) is a closed, self-administered medical aid scheme serving South African municipal workers — roughly 35,000 members and 73,000 covered lives. It collects about R1.9 billion/year in contributions, kept reserves over R1.3 billion and posted a R14.3 million surplus in 2024 (solvency 68% vs the 25% legal minimum). Plans are income-banded and cheap (from ~R750/month with a 60% employer subsidy), covering hospitals, doctors, medication, dentistry and optics. Led by Principal Officer Francina Mosoeu with a union-appointed board, it administers benefits with Medscheme across a network of private hospital groups. Key problems right now: membership shrinking ~15%/year as young people leave, and an ongoing court battle with the Melomed hospital group over contract exclusions — plus the long-term threat of national health insurance reform.

edcon.co.za zoominfo.com/c/edcon/36900910 Edcon (roots from 1929, Johannesburg) was South Africa's largest non-food retailer — owner of iconic chains Edgars, Jet, CNA and Boardmans, with ~1,200 stores across Southern Africa, ~19,000 staff, revenue of R25+ billion and four million private-label credit cards. It was crippled by Bain Capital's 2007 leveraged buyout (~R25 billion), losing market share to discounters before COVID-19 lockdown wiped out R2 billion in sales and forced business rescue in April 2020. The group was then broken up: Jet was sold to The Foschini Group (~R480m), Edgars to Retailability (~R350m, 5,200 jobs saved), CNA and credit books to other buyers. The Edcon holding company itself no longer trades — edcon.co.za is now a business-rescue notice board where practitioners Marsden and Schapiro distribute sale proceeds to creditors (payments started September 2024, proceedings still open as of 2025).
